original_question: For finite-rank unitary perturbations of rank n > 1, extend the classical proof of the equivalence between an inner characteristic operator function and purely singular spectrum to the higher-rank setting, and use that extension to derive explicit density formulas for the absolutely continuous part of the spectral measure.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1 (Introduction), read together with the immediately following Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3: the finite-rank Aleksandrov-Clark/Clark-operator extension problem for non-inner characteristic operator functions.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s finite-rank unitary-perturbation setting, the central inner-characteristic-function versus purely singular-spectrum theme, and the fact that the rank-one non-inner Clark theory is the model one wants to extend to higher rank. It also correctly notices that explicit formulas for the absolutely continuous part of the spectral measure are tied to that Clark-theoretic extension.
missing_details: The ambient setting should be a completely nonunitary contraction on a separable complex Hilbert space, not just an abstract finite-rank unitary perturbation problem.
The defect/deficiency indices must be equal and finite, namely (n,n) with n>1.
The perturbations in question are the rank-n unitary Aleksandrov-Clark perturbations parametrized by a unitary n x n operator/matrix acting between identified defect spaces.
The characteristic object is the operator-valued Sz.-Nagy-Foias characteristic function Θ, analytic on the unit disk; the draft does not specify this.
"Inner" must be interpreted in the operator-valued sense: the nontangential boundary values of Θ are unitary almost everywhere on the unit circle.

"Purely singular spectrum" must be tied to the spectral/Aleksandrov-Clark measures of the unitary perturbations, i.e. zero absolutely continuous part with respect to Lebesgue measure on the unit circle.
The draft omits the quantifier: the paper-faithful formulation concerns the whole family of rank-n unitary perturbations/Clark measures, not an unspecified single perturbation.

The paper’s nearby official formulation is not a stand-alone theorem already asserting higher-rank density formulas; rather, Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 supply the rank-one non-inner formulas that motivate the higher-rank extension.
The "classical proof" to be extended is specifically the Clark-operator / normalized-Cauchy-transform argument from rank one, not merely any alternative proof of innerness versus singularity.
If one asks for density formulas in higher rank, they should be matrix-valued Radon-Nikodym formulas for the absolutely continuous part of the corresponding spectral/Clark measures.
refined_question: Let T be a completely nonunitary contraction on a separable complex Hilbert space with equal finite defect indices (n,n), where n>1, and let Θ_T be its operator-valued Sz.-Nagy-Foias characteristic function. Can one develop a finite-rank Aleksandrov-Clark theory for the family of rank-n unitary perturbations of T that extends the classical rank-one Clark-operator proof to the non-inner operator-valued setting—namely, obtain a higher-rank analogue of the rank-one formulas in Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 for the adjoint Clark operator/normalized Cauchy transform, and from it recover by a Clark-theoretic argument that Θ_T is inner if and only if the corresponding unitary perturbations have purely singular spectral measures, together with explicit matrix-valued Radon-Nikodym formulas for the absolutely continuous parts of those measures?
justification: The draft is aimed at the opening higher-rank Clark-theory problem in the paper, not at a broader perturbation-theory program. In the introduction, Conjecture 1.1 is the nearest official formulation, while Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 record the rank-one non-inner formulas whose finite-rank extension is being sought. So the paper-faithful sharpening must keep the c.n.u. hypothesis, the equal defect-index hypothesis, the operator-valued characteristic function Θ_T, the family of rank-n unitary Aleksandrov-Clark perturbations, and the precise meanings of "inner" and "purely singular." Your draft is close in mathematical intent, but it merges the official higher-rank conjectural target with the nearby rank-one supporting results and leaves several hidden hypotheses and quantifiers unstated.
